key_insight: Matrix-structured optimizers, especially SOAP and SOAP-Muon, can train ML interatomic potentials faster and to better accuracy than Adam, making optimizer choice a major but previously underexplored lever.
engineering_relevance: For scientific ML practitioners building NequIP or Allegro models, swapping the optimizer can materially improve convergence and label efficiency, especially when force labels are limited.
method: Compared Adam against Muon, SOAP, and SOAP-Muon.
Trained NequIP and Allegro MLIP models under standard and partial force-supervision settings.
Evaluated convergence speed and final accuracy across optimizer choices.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic comparisons showing SOAP and SOAP-Muon consistently outperform Adam, with especially strong gains under partial force supervision.
watch_item: These gains may depend on model family, hyperparameter tuning, and the specific supervision regime, so implementation details matter when transferring the results to new MLIP setups.
paper_title: Beyond Adam: SOAP and Muon for Faster, Label-Efficient Training of Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
